text:
alex: Heads-up — CI on main is red across sequencer tests after the image bump that landed ~4 hours ago. Can someone help find last-green so we can bisect? :thinking:

ci-bot: Buildkite failed: https://buildkite.com/redwood/infra/builds/5821 (job: sequencer-integration) — failing step `sequencer_shard_test` — exit code 1

maria: I saw that too. PR #987 updated the sequencer runtime image tag. Could be the image or a dependent change. Worth a quick rerun to rule out flake.

derek: @alex can you paste the failing log snippet?

alex: sure, cropped log: ```
E   AssertionError: sequence shard mismatch
E   Expected: 128
E   Actual: 64
...
Command: ./run_integ --test sequencer_shard_test
```

jen: happy to kick off a bisect if we have a good candidate last-green. If the image changed, we might need to bisect both the repo and the image tag.

sam: I can try a quick rerun now to check flakiness, re-triggering buildkite job.

ci-bot: Re-run triggered: https://buildkite.com/redwood/infra/builds/5822 (rebuild of 5821)

sam: rerun also failed, same assertion. Not flaky.

maria: PR #987 shows image tag moved from sha: 3f1a9b2 -> b7c4d11. If we revert to 3f1a9b2 locally and run the same job, that should tell us if image introduced it.

alex: I tried locally with 3f1a9b2 and the test passed once. So that narrows it to the image.

derek: Good narrowing. For audit/rollout we still should find last-green commit in main in case other changes interact. @jen do you want me to run git bisect with the image pinned?

jen: Yes — start with bad=HEAD, good=<last-green-commit>. If we don't know last-green, we can query the CI history for the last successful sequencer-integration job before the image bump timestamp.

sam: quick lookup shows a successful build at 1965428000 (build 5798) — that was before the image bump merge. commit hash on that build: c4b2e8f1

alex: thanks. So `good=c4b2e8f1` and `bad=HEAD`.

jen: plan: 1) Derek will run repo bisect with image pinned to b7c4d11 to see if repo change contributes. 2) If bisect is all good, we revert image in infra for a hotfix and coordinate a new image roll. 3) File a follow-up with PR #987 author.

derek: Starting bisect now. Command I'm using: 
```
git bisect start HEAD c4b2e8f1
# build script that pins image tag and runs sequencer_integration
./ci/run_bisect_build.sh --image b7c4d11
```

alex: ping me if you hit a flaky step that blocks automation. I'll help triage manually.

ci-bot: bisect job queued: https://buildkite.com/redwood/infra/builds/5823 (will post results in thread)

sam: also notifying release infra to hold any further sequencer image promotions until we know more — @maria please ack if that's ok.

maria: ack. Holding promos.

jen: if bisect points to image-only, let's do emergency revert of the image tag in staging/infra and then stage a rollback PR for prod. I'll draft the revert PR and assign to @alex for merge once CI green.

derek: first bisect run finished: suspect commit is 7a9d1c4 (touches sequencer kv encoding). Re-running to confirm.

alex: interesting — that commit predates the image bump?

derek: yes 7a9d1c4 is from two days ago, merged before image PR. Combined with image change seems to expose the mismatch. Need a reproducer to be sure.

maria: can we run a matrix: (old-image + 7a9d1c4) and (new-image + earlier commit) to see if it's additive?

jen: good call. Derek, can you run those two quick combinations?

derek: on it. Running both now.

ci-bot: matrix runs started: https://buildkite.com/redwood/infra/builds/5824

sam: thanks all. Once we have matrix result, we can decide whether to revert image, revert commit 7a9d1c4, or produce a patch. Keep this thread updated. :eyes:
